Leadership & Organization

Cognitive Inequality

An unequal ability to control, understand, or benefit from AI systems, which leaves some people directing AI and others dependent on it.

Explanation

Cognitive inequality, sometimes discussed as part of a broader 'cognitive divide' or 'AI divide', describes disparities that go beyond simple access to technology (the older digital divide) to differences in who can shape, question, and control the AI systems that increasingly mediate perception and decision-making, versus who is simply subject to them. Academic literature frames this as a multidimensional issue combining technological, institutional, and psychological factors, including the risk that some users treat AI as a genuine cognitive extension while others become dependent on it as a crutch. For marketers and organizations, this affects how confidently different customer or employee segments engage with AI-powered products and raises questions about equitable design of AI tools.

Usage context / examples

A company rolling out an AI assistant to all employees may find that some teams use it to genuinely extend their thinking while others become passively dependent on it, widening internal skill gaps over time.

Related terms

Digital divide, AI divide, digital literacy

Turkish equivalent

Bilişsel eşitsizlik, yapay zeka sistemlerini yönlendirebilenlerle bu sistemlere bağımlı hale gelenler arasındaki, erişimin ötesine geçen kontrol ve anlama farkını ifade eder.
